wind.status: NEW 2026-10-19 (owner: there was no wind noise; the sound heard as wind was the tyre layer). Every number is [AS] unless stated.
wind.level_note: Aerodynamic sound from turbulent flow over a body is a dipole/boundary-layer source: sound power ~ U^5 ... U^6 (Lighthill 1952, 'On sound generated aerodynamically I': monopole U^4, dipole U^6, quadrupole U^8; Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles, aeroacoustics chapter: 50-60 log10 U). 50 dB per decade is the low end of that range: 15 dB per doubling of the airspeed. rms_at_reference is chosen so wind and tyre noise are equally loud at about 130 km/h: tyre dominates in town, wind on the motorway and above.
wind.centre_note: Strouhal-type scaling f = St * U / L: the spectrum's weight moves up proportionally with the airspeed
